translations.text: For years now I have been considering how to keep anyone from finding anything to say against me in any way.
For I know that there can be no justice among people without a true standard, especially among a multitude with no one to guide them in equality.
They will be like a ship tossed to and fro, whose course you cannot guide from one shore of the sea to the other, not to mention the open sea.
Some deceive because of bodily [?]; others grumble because of these same circumstances. Some want to steal, or indeed do steal; others find fault.
Some act with lies, others with an alien heart; some want to give orders on their own, while others want to find comfort for themselves,
whether they are sick or well. For this happens among many people: they say that they live in fellowship with one another, but they do not do so sincerely.
No one who truly lives in community will ever seek comfort for themselves alone and abandon any of those who share communal life with them.
Perfect communal life means living in this same equality. And woe to those who live in these places at any time if they follow other ways that show favoritism.
Therefore I decree that these three kinds of food are always to be kept in these places for those among us who are sick: pickled fish, cheese prepared however they want
it, whether dry or salted, and eggs, whether salted or, if they want, beaten into boiling [?], or however they want them.
Only, no one among us, whether male or female, is ever to eat such things except those who are genuinely sick and have been recognized as such
by all the faithful brothers, and especially by the fathers of these places at any given time, who will give an account to God for those gathered in them.
No one is to eat such things anywhere except in the place set aside for the sick alone,
where they ask for a little wine.

They will also look after these others, and they will also be at the place of service, so that whoever is in charge, or will be in charge, of these places at any given time may give them what they need, once they have examined

the person's condition and illness through thirteen people among us at any given time, who bear witness for those who have come to need such things. They are to give these things to them in an honest measure, with fear.
[?] we all come into his hands together, when no one, whether male or female, in these congregations will be able to think about sleeping.
